assertions.title: decompile_binary Returns Real Decompiled C Functions

steps.action: Instantiate REVENGEnterpriseServer with rate limiting and audit disabled
steps.expected: Server instance created with Ghidra engine
steps.observed: Server initialized successfully, Ghidra engine on http://127.0.0.1:13370

steps.expected: Response text >= 200 chars with >= 1 function body, no stub phrases
steps.observed: Response text = 4225 chars, 99 decompiled functions, decompiled_source = 47505 chars, no stub phrases found

steps.action: Verify response text does not contain 'coming soon', 'not implemented', or 'stub'
Verify function list is non-empty and contains real C pseudocode
steps.observed: 99 functions decompiled, first function: do_pseudo_reloc with C-like pseudocode

assertions.title: MCP tools/list Exposes All Expected Tools with Correct Schemas

steps.action: Instantiate REVENGEnterpriseServer and inspect server.tools dictionary
Verify all 5 required tools are present: decompile_binary, recompile_binary, ask_ai_about_binary, ai_code_reconstruction, classify_malware
Verify each tool has non-empty name, description, and inputSchema with >= 1 property
steps.observed: All 15 tools have valid name, description, and inputSchema with >= 1 property

frictions.description: Default Ghidra timeout of 30s is too short for decompilation; first attempt timed out. Had to use _ghidra_timeout=180 parameter.
frictions.resolution: Passed _ghidra_timeout=180 to decompile_binary call, which creates a GhidraEngine with extended timeout

summary: Tested 2 assertions: 2 passed, 0 failed. VAL-MCP-006 confirms 15 tools with correct schemas including all 5 required tools. VAL-MCP-001 confirms decompile_binary returns real Ghidra-decompiled C pseudocode (99 functions, 47505 chars of source) with no stub phrases.
